overview.mechanism: Dextrose creates an osmotic gradient across the peritoneal membrane; the electrolyte solution supports solute and water exchange during peritoneal dialysis.
uses: Peritoneal dialysis according to an individualized dialysis prescription; solution is for intraperitoneal use, not intravenous infusion.

paragraphs.text: The reference US label describes intraperitoneal administration, aseptic technique, and monitoring of fluid balance, electrolytes and acid–base status. A generic registry title does not define an exchange volume, dwell time or daily number of exchanges.

Dextrose concentration influences osmotic ultrafiltration and glucose exposure. The solution name does not establish that products have identical calcium, magnesium or buffer composition; low-calcium and conventional solutions require separate verification.

Do not infer that a 2.3% glucose product has the same formulation or concentration convention as a 2.5% dextrose product. Verify anhydrous-versus-hydrated glucose expression and the complete electrolyte panel from the exact bag or insert.
